messages:
Olivia: kicking off post-bake nightwatch for kernel+quant build 2026-03-20. pushed the staging image and started thermal-sim. please watch canaries.
Raj: noticed a small p95 token-time bump in eu-west canary at ~02:12 UTC, still under SLO but trending.
Tim: digging into thermal-sim output — spikes correlate with sequences >1024 tokens, KV cache reuse pattern looks off. not in short-smoke.
Maria: re: release notes, the packing change needs a line about ABI compatibility and that older drivers will fallback to scalar path. i can add it if you confirm the wording.
Olivia: yes add a note: "quant pack v3 toggles on a fused matmul kernel; fallback to v2 supported but incurs ~12% perf regression". keep short.
Tim: also attaching the failing snippet from staging logs:
```
ERROR runtime: unexpected kernel assertion at matmul_fused.cpp:128
context: seq_len=2048, dtype=q4_0, device=cuX
```
Raj: that assertion only reproducible when batch contains mix of short+long sequences. maybe batching algo needs guard.
Olivia: ok, ops/qa: hold the public rollout. we're going to keep traffic at 10% canary, no cross-region ramp until fix or mitigation.
qa-bot: smoke results: 50/50 pass/fail on long-seq tests; failing cases show slightly higher memory transient and occasional assertion above.
Tim: mitigation options: 1) throttle batching for mixed-length requests (quick config), 2) pin long-seq customers to engine:v2 legacy for next 24h, 3) rollback kernel bundle and re-run bake.
Raj: preference for opt #2 + batching guard. pinning is fastest low-risk. Ops, can we pin tenants with seq>1024?
Olivia: ops: yes we can apply route pin for affected customer ids. Deploy-bot, create a sticky pin for engine:v2 on tenant list: alpha/omega/test-legal.
deploy-bot: created pin sticky: engine:v2 for tenants [alpha, omega, test-legal], ttl=24h, reason="nightwatch thermal regression - long sequences" :white_check_mark:
Maria: i've updated release-notes draft with the ABI/pack note and a callout about long-sequence caveat. pushed PR #402.
Olivia: rollback criteria we agreed on: (a) >5% increase in error rate on canary aggregates OR (b) sustained p95 latency +20% over baseline for 15m OR (c) thermal-sim shows device temp crossing safety threshold. if any hit, trigger full rollback.
Tim: adding a metric watch: alert group "nightwatch-thermalsim" -> alert if p95 delta >=20% OR errors increase >=5% within 15m.
Raj: I'll keep a manual eye on eu-west and us-central canaries. tagging oncall.
Olivia: thanks. final plan: hold at 10% canary, pin high-risk tenants to engine:v2, deploy batching guard config to staging, update release notes PR, re-run thermal-sim for long sequences overnight. reconvene 3479990365 UTC or earlier if alerts.
Tim: ack, will post any logs here if new hits show.
Maria: acked, PR up, will follow up on changelog merge.
Olivia: thanks team, if no alerts by reconvene time we start 25% ramp next day AM. :thumbsup:
